clips.prompt: A right-handed tennis player waits on the baseline in an athletic ready stance: feet wider than the shoulders, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet, both hands held together in front of the waist as if holding a racket, bouncing lightly and shifting weight from foot to foot.

A tennis player stands relaxed between points, catching his breath, rolling his shoulders and shifting his weight, the right hand loose at the side as if holding a racket, the left hand on the hip for a moment.
A tennis player in a ready stance makes one small hop with both feet, lands wide with bent knees and balanced, both hands in front of the waist.
A tennis player runs forward in a straight line at a fast pace with short quick steps, leaning slightly forward, the right hand held in front of the body as if holding a racket, the left arm pumping.
A tennis player shuffles sideways to his right with quick side steps, feet never crossing, knees bent and low, chest facing forward the whole time, both hands in front of the waist.
A tennis player shuffles sideways to his left with quick side steps, feet never crossing, knees bent and low, chest facing forward the whole time, both hands in front of the waist.
A tennis player backpedals straight backwards with quick short steps while still facing forward, knees bent, both hands in front of the chest.

A right-handed tennis player hits a forehand groundstroke: turns his shoulders to the right, takes the right arm back low behind the body, steps in with the left foot, then swings the right arm forward and up across the body in a fast low-to-high stroke and finishes with the right hand over the left shoulder.

A right-handed tennis player hits a two-handed backhand groundstroke: turns his shoulders to the left with both hands together on the left side, steps in with the right foot, then swings both arms forward and up across the body in a fast low-to-high stroke and finishes with both hands high over the right shoulder.

A right-handed tennis player serves: stands sideways, tosses the ball straight up with the left hand while bending the knees and arching the back with the right arm cocked behind the head, then drives up off both feet, reaches high and swings the right arm up and over to strike the ball overhead, and follows through down across the left side of the body, landing on the left foot.

A right-handed tennis player at the net hits a short forehand volley: takes a small step forward with the left foot and punches the right hand forward and slightly down in front of the body with a short firm motion, then recovers to a ready stance.

A right-handed tennis player at the net hits a short backhand volley: turns the shoulders slightly left, steps forward with the right foot and punches the right hand forward across the front of the body on the left side with a short firm motion, then recovers to a ready stance.

A right-handed tennis player hits an overhead smash: turns sideways, points the left hand up at a high ball, takes the right arm back behind the head, then jumps slightly and swings the right arm hard up and down over the head and follows through across the body.
A tennis player celebrates winning a point: clenches the right fist and pumps it twice in front of the chest, then turns and walks a couple of steps.
